title: Progressive Role Editing with Inline Audit & Impact Preview
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Overview: Design a progressive-disclosure role editor in the Console that allows admins to make incremental role changes while seeing an inline preview of the resulting audit log entries and the effective permission impact on members and resources. The goal is to reduce risky bulk edits by surfacing: (1) how a change alters effective permissions across namespace/resource scopes, (2) which members gain/lose access, (3) the exact audit log entry that will be recorded (including fields required for compliance), and (4) an estimated risk/categorization tag for the change.

Scope: UI/UX flows for role editing and member assignment only. Not in this ticket: deep backend evaluation engine (ENG tasks will surface effective perms), SSO mapping changes, or multi-tenant policy rollout engine. This work must integrate with existing audit schema and RBAC v2 model.

Why: Current role edits are opaque: admins often perform bulk updates, discover regressions later in audits, or over-provision privileges. Providing a preview reduces errors, supports safer rollouts (canary edits), and creates consistent audit records required by compliance teams.

Core features:
- Inline permission delta preview: a compact diff that shows additions/removals grouped by permission category (read/write/admin) and resource scope.
- Member impact list: top 5 affected users/teams with quick jump links to expand full list.
- Audit entry simulator: shows the final audit log JSON that will be emitted, including actor, timestamp (simulated), before/after snapshots, change rationale field, and whether the change will be marked as automated or manual.
- Staged commits: option to save as Draft, Apply Now, or Apply Gradually (canary rollout to selected cohorts).
- Safety checks and warnings: highlight policy violations, privilege escalation risks, and conflicts with SSO group mappings.
- Lightweight heatmap: risk score per resource group and an overall change severity badge (low/medium/high).
- Undo/rollback path: link to create an explicit rollback ticket with prefilled diffs saved to the audit trail.

User journeys covered:
1) Admin adjusts a role permission -> sees delta preview + member impact -> fixes a risky permission -> applies change and confirms audit entry.
2) Platform engineer prepares a canary rollout -> chooses 10% of org -> monitors Console telemetry and applies wider rollout.
3) Compliance reviewer reviews the simulated audit on draft changes before approval.

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity mockups for desktop + tablet of the role edit canvas, inline preview panel, and commit modal.
- Component specs for the delta list, member impact stream, and audit simulator card.
- Accessibility checklist and keyboard flows.
- Hand-off notes for ENG: required backend endpoints and contract for effective permission evaluation and canary rollout API.

Non-goals: automated remediation suggestions (outside scope), server-side role merge heuristics, or full policy authoring UI.
acceptance_criteria: When editing a role, the UI shows a clear per-permission delta (added/removed/modified) grouped by category
Member impact panel lists top affected members and exposes full list on demand
Audit simulator renders the exact audit payload fields that will be written and marks required compliance fields
Admins can choose Draft / Apply Now / Apply Gradually and the chosen action is present in the outgoing API call payload
Warnings are shown for privilege escalation and SSO mapping conflicts; applying a change with critical warnings requires explicit confirmation
Design artifacts include responsive mocks, component specs, and an accessibility checklist

Design handoff includes a clear list of backend contracts (endpoints, inputs, outputs) and performance expectations for permission evaluation (target < 400ms for 90th percentile on small-to-medium orgs)
decisions: Use progressive disclosure: keep main role editor compact and surface the full impact preview in a collapsible right rail
Audit simulator will mirror the exact production audit schema; we will not invent a separate preview format
Canary rollout is limited to percentage-based cohorts and explicit user/team pick lists; staging will be handled by the backend
Only admins with 'role.apply' grant can bypass warnings; other editors can create Drafts for reviewer approval
tradeoffs: Performance vs. completeness: computing full effective permissions for very large orgs is expensive. We will compute a sampled preview for >10k principals and show a notice explaining sampling
Cognitive load: showing too much detail may overwhelm users. We prioritize top-level deltas and an expandable member list rather than full permission matrices by default

Implementation complexity: canary rollout and staged commits require coordination with Dedicated and Private control planes, increasing scope—initial implementation will support Console-managed cohorts only
engineering_notes: Required endpoints: POST /rbac/v2/evaluate-delta (input: proposed_role_changes, sample_size), POST /rbac/v2/preview-audit (input: change_payload), POST /rbac/v2/commit-role-change (input: commit_type, rollout_options)
Backend must return: permission_deltas (list), affected_principals_sample (list), estimated_risk_score (string), simulated_audit_payload (stringified JSON)
Performance target: delta evaluation for orgs <10k principals should return <400ms on p95. For larger orgs return sampled results and a processing job link
Feature flag: rbac.v2.progressive_preview, start disabled in Private deployments until migration guide is ready
Privacy: simulated audit payload must not include sensitive tokens; follow existing audit sanitization rules
